doc.title: Dianne Reeves interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, October 13, 2001

title: Billy Childs and the arrangements, especially 'Send In the Clowns'
summary: Longtime friend Billy Childs arranged the album; they discussed lyrics and mood, working hardest on 'Send In the Clowns'.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Impeccable arrangements. Really creative. You know people are always talking about trying to make the strings swing? Well someone did there.

Billy Childs. I’ve known Billy for a long time. We started working together when we were about 19 years old and our relationship is very, very rich and musically we shared a lot of music together. So when this project came about I asked him would he do the arrangements and he’s like yeah. So we would get together and have cappuccino and talk about the songs. Because it wasn’t so much that I wanted to select the songs —she sang so many songs. Sarah sang so many songs. I wanted to really celebrate her artistry, her approach to the music. And so there had to be some certain things that were in the arrangements and I remember he was nervous when we first started and George told him, “Man you know her like you know the palm of your hand so do what you do.” And it was great. And he wrote incredible arrangements.
I’m curious, some of the really hip substitutions that were used on like “Lullaby of Birdland” and stuff, did you two sit down and maybe he would try things and say do you like this?

Exactly. It was funny because I was touring a lot at the time that we were working on the music and — Billy understands a lot of times that when I’m singing certain things, certain harmonies, certain feelings that I want to project, the harmonies have a lot to do with that, with the poetry of the music I guess, with the lyrics of the music. So we’d sit down and we would talk about different things. I think the thing that we really worked very hard on was “Send In the Clowns.” That was, because Sarah’s version was just so spectacular, we knew that whatever was going to be done with that song had to be uniquely my own. And so we’d sit down and we would work on things and discuss the lyrics, discuss the mood, discuss the feeling, all of these things. And then he would write accordingly.
